program_name: Federal 9% Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (Competitive)
administering_agency: California Tax Credit Allocation Committee (CTCAC), State Treasurer's Office
typical_award_size: 2026 federal ceiling $136.4M annual credit statewide ($3.416 per capita). Per-project cap $2.8M annual federal credit (Reg. 10325(f)(9)(C)). Set-asides: Nonprofit 10%, Rural 20% (incl. 14% RHS/HOME/CDBG-DR and 10% Native American apportionments within rural), At-Risk 5%, Special Needs 4%. Geographic apportionments for target counties: Capital Region (El Dorado, Placer, Sacramento, Sutter, Yuba, Yolo) 5.7%; East Bay (Alameda, Contra Costa) 7.4%; South and West Bay (San Mateo, Santa Clara) 6.0%; Northern Region (Butte, Marin, Napa, Shasta, Solano, Sonoma) 4.4%; Central Valley (incl. San Joaquin) 8.6%.
per_unit_cap: No fixed per-unit cap; credit limited by threshold basis limits (updated Jan 2026) and $2.8M annual federal credit per project. Developer fee cap $2.5M generally.
affordability_requirement: Minimum federal 20% at 50% AMI or 40% at 60% AMI (or average income test); competitive scoring effectively requires deep targeting. 55-year CTCAC regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: 2026 rounds closed (R1 April 7, 2026; R2 July 21, 2026). 2027 schedule not posted as of 2026-11-06; expect two rounds, spring and summer 2027. 2027 regulations to be adopted Dec 9, 2026.
layering_notes: Mutually exclusive with 4% credits and CDLAC bonds on the same building; a project may not hold concurrent 9% and 4% AHSC applications. Commonly stacked with HCD MHP, AHSC, VHHP, Serna, local HOME/CDBG, county and city soft loans, and the welfare property tax exemption. CTCAC awards state credits alongside 9% federal credits via geographic apportionments (state credits adjusted at 80%). Nonprofit set-aside prioritizes homeless-assistance projects with at least $500K or $10K/unit of MHP, VHHP, Homekey, NPLH, HHC or MHSA capital. Prevailing wage not required by CTCAC itself, but Reg. 10327 grants a 20% threshold basis limit increase for prevailing-wage projects and 5% more for a PLA or skilled-and-trained workforce. Tiebreaker favors high public leverage, so local soft money matters. Max four awards per applicant per round. Proposed 2027 changes (Dec 9, 2026 adoption) would let small regions access the full annual apportionment in round 1 and cap state credit requests at $150,000 per tax credit unit.

program_name: Federal 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (Tax-Exempt Bond Financed)
administering_agency: California Tax Credit Allocation Committee (CTCAC), joint application with CDLAC
typical_award_size: Non-competitive at CTCAC once CDLAC bond allocation is secured; credit equals roughly 4% of qualified basis annually for 10 years, limited by threshold basis limits. No per-project federal credit cap. Application fee $1,500 CTCAC plus $1,500 CDLAC ($1,700 scattered-site or resyndication).
per_unit_cap: None stated; governed by threshold basis limits and CDLAC bond sizing.
affordability_requirement: Federal minimum 20% at 50% AMI or 40% at 60% AMI (average income test allowed); CDLAC scoring drives deeper targeting. 55-year regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: 2026 joint CDLAC/CTCAC rounds closed (Feb 3, May 19, Sept 8, 2026). 2027 schedule not posted as of 2026-11-06; expect three rounds (early Feb, mid May, early Sept pattern).
layering_notes: Requires CDLAC private activity bond allocation (bond financing threshold reduced from 50% to 25% of aggregate basis plus land by federal H.R. 1 for bonds issued after 2025). Core stack for larger new construction: 4% credits + CDLAC bonds + state credits (base or enhanced) + HCD MHP or AHSC + CalHFA MIP + local soft funds. Enhanced state credits ($500M program) available only with 4% new construction. Acq/rehab 4% deals can access the 15% state credit set-aside. Cannot combine with 9% credits on the same building. CalHFA bond recycling can substitute for part of the bond allocation but recycled bonds do not generate 4% credits. Prevailing wage is not triggered by the credits or conduit bonds alone, but most state soft sources in the stack (HCD, AHSC) will trigger it; CTCAC gives a 20% basis limit boost for prevailing wage projects.

program_name: State Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (Base Program, R&TC Sec. (g)(1)(A))
administering_agency: California Tax Credit Allocation Committee (CTCAC)
typical_award_size: 2026 state credit ceiling $129.6M ($70M statutory base plus CPI adjustment), of which $67.3M available in 2026 after prior-year advance allocations. 15% ($10.1M) set aside for 4% acquisition/rehab projects; balance awarded with 9% credits through geographic apportionments. State credit is taken over 4 years (30% of basis for new construction: 9%/9%/9%/3%; 13% for acq/rehab basis). Separate $500K annual Farmworker credit.
per_unit_cap: Proposed 2027 regulation caps state credit requests at $150,000 per tax credit unit (currently $200,000); farmworker projects exempt.
affordability_requirement: Same as paired federal credit; state credit available only to projects receiving or concurrently receiving federal LIHTC. 55-year regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: Awarded in the same 9% and 4% rounds; 2027 round schedule not posted as of 2026-11-06.
layering_notes: Paired with 9% credits automatically in geographic apportionments (CTCAC may exchange state credits for federal credits if state credits run short; proposed 2027 rule keeps at least 50% of the state request). 4% acq/rehab projects can request state credits only from the 15% set-aside and must meet criteria (A)-(D): building at least 15 years old, serving very low or extremely low income averaging 45% AMI or RHS 514/521 financed, insufficient credits due to low appraised value, substantial rehab. State credits may be certificated (sold) by nonprofit applicants at no less than $0.80 per dollar. Does not count as public funds for prevailing wage.

program_name: Enhanced State Tax Credits for 4% New Construction (R&TC Sec. (g)(1)(B), $500M program)
administering_agency: California Tax Credit Allocation Committee (CTCAC)
typical_award_size: $500M in state credits per year (2020 through 2026 budgets), plus carryforward ($515.5M total in 2026). 2026 split: $390.5M general allocation across the three 4% rounds, $25M for farmworker housing, $100M reserved for CalHFA Mixed-Income Program projects (used in Round 2). Basis multiplier 30% of construction-related basis (75% for projects not otherwise eligible for the 130% boost).
per_unit_cap: Proposed 2027 cap of $150,000 state credit per tax credit unit.
affordability_requirement: New construction paired with 4% federal credits; must receive a CDLAC bond allocation. Ranking follows CDLAC pools and set-asides (Rural, Homeless, ELI/VLI, Mixed-Income, geographic regions).
next_deadline: Awarded with CDLAC/CTCAC 4% rounds; 2027 appropriation subject to the 2027-28 state budget (program has been funded annually since 2020). 2027 round dates not posted as of 2026-11-06.
layering_notes: This is the main gap filler for 4% new construction deals and is the credit source CalHFA MIP relies on ($100M MIP set-aside, which CTCAC may cut to $200M statutory max or lower by agreement). Not available for acq/rehab or 9% projects. State credits are allocated by CDLAC pool ranking when oversubscribed: Emerging Developer (replacing BIPOC) 15%, Rural 15%, Homeless set-aside 25%, ELI/VLI set-aside 20%, then geographic regions. Beginning 2028, the $25M farmworker credits would pair with HDFC's Joe Serna program under proposed rules.

program_name: State Farmworker Housing Tax Credit
administering_agency: California Tax Credit Allocation Committee (CTCAC)
typical_award_size: $500,000 in new state credits annually (plus carryforward; $1.0M available and fully awarded in 2026). Separate $25M annual enhanced state credit set-aside for 4% farmworker new construction. Basis multiplier up to 75% for farmworker projects.
affordability_requirement: Farmworker housing meeting CTCAC definition; paired with federal credits.
next_deadline: Awarded in regular CTCAC rounds; 2027 schedule not posted as of 2026-11-06.
layering_notes: Relevant to agricultural counties in scope (Napa, Sonoma, Yolo, San Joaquin, Solano). Commonly paired with HCD Joe Serna Jr. Farmworker Housing Grant and USDA Section 514/516. Exempt from the proposed per-unit state credit cap.

program_name: State Historic Rehabilitation Tax Credit
administering_agency: Office of Historic Preservation (OHP) with CTCAC (allocation and regulations)
typical_award_size: $50M annual statewide: $40M for projects with QREs of $1M or more, $8M for projects under $1M, $2M for residences (capped $25,000 each). Credit is 20% of qualified rehabilitation expenditures, 25% for projects meeting criteria in Appendix D of the application instructions (includes affordable housing categories).
affordability_requirement: None required for the base 20% credit; 25% tier criteria include affordable housing. Properties must be listed or eligible for the California or National Register.
next_deadline: OHP states funding for all categories is exhausted and applications are not being accepted; new allocations would be announced on the OHP page. Verify in early 2027.
layering_notes: Pairs with the federal 20% historic credit for dual projects and with LIHTC for adaptive reuse of historic buildings. CTCAC regulations for this credit effective Nov 12, 2024; CTCAC approved initial allocations April 8, June 18 and Sept 30, 2025.

program_name: Qualified Residential Rental Project (QRRP) Tax-Exempt Private Activity Bond Allocation
administering_agency: California Debt Limit Allocation Committee (CDLAC), State Treasurer's Office
typical_award_size: 2026 state ceiling $5.31B, QRRP share $4.77B (plus $56M carryforward). Non-geographic pools $3.0B: Acquisition and Rehabilitation $1.0B, BIPOC $130M, Rural new construction $130M, Homeless set-aside $650M, ELI/VLI set-aside $780M, State-funded Mixed Income $310M. New construction geographic apportionments $1.75B: Bay Area Region 21%, Northern Region 9%, Inland Region 16%, Coastal 21%, City of LA 17%, Balance of LA 16%. Supplemental pool $79.7M. Application fee $1,500; performance deposit 0.5% of allocation up to $100,000; allocation fee 0.035% of bond amount.
per_unit_cap: None; bond sizing driven by CDLAC scoring and tiebreaker (public benefit per dollar of bonds plus state credits).
affordability_requirement: Federal minimum 20% at 50% AMI or 40% at 60% AMI (with 10% at 50% AMI under CalHFA issuance). ELI/VLI set-aside requires average 50% AMI or below plus an HCD or similar award. Mixed Income set-aside for projects with 50% or fewer restricted units or in CalHFA MIP. 55-year CDLAC regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: 2026 rounds closed (Feb 3, May 19, Sept 8, 2026; Round 3 awards Dec 9, 2026). 2027 schedule not posted as of 2026-11-06. 2027 regulations proposed for adoption Dec 9, 2026 (replaces BIPOC pool with Emerging Developer pool).
layering_notes: Prerequisite for 4% federal credits and enhanced state credits; applications are joint with CTCAC through the CDLAC online portal. Readiness points require construction start within 180, 201 or 222 days of allocation and committed soft financing at application, so HCD, AHSC, MIP and local awards must be in hand first. Bonds generally sized to at least 25% of aggregate basis plus land (federal threshold after H.R. 1; prior 50% test). CalHFA recycled bonds and 501(c)(3) bonds do not use volume cap. Conduit bond financing alone is generally not treated as public funds for state prevailing wage, but confirm with counsel; most paired state soft funds do trigger it. Issuers in target counties include CalHFA, CSCDA, CMFA, and local housing authorities.

program_name: Mixed-Income Program (MIP)
administering_agency: California Housing Finance Agency (CalHFA); transitioning to Housing Development and Finance Committee (HDFC) under the California Housing and Homelessness Agency
typical_award_size: 2026 round: $63M in subsidy loans to 13 developments (1,768 units); funded by 15% of SB 2 Building Homes and Jobs Act revenue. Per project: lesser of $6M, $50,000 per MIP-regulated unit ($60,000 in High or Highest Resource areas), or 50% of the CalHFA permanent loan. Sponsor limited to one award per year; no county may receive more than 25% of annual funds; age-restricted projects capped at 25%.
per_unit_cap: $50,000 per MIP-regulated unit; $60,000 in High/Highest Resource areas
affordability_requirement: New construction, 4% credits with income averaging; at least 51% LIHTC units. MIP regulatory agreement (55 years): 30% of units at or below 50% AMI (including 10% at or below 30% AMI), 10% of units at 60% to 80% AMI averaging 70%, remaining units at or below 120% AMI; spread between lowest and highest targets at least 40 points; average affordability no more than 60% AMI. Rents at least 10% below market.
next_deadline: 2026 round closed (application workbook due March 2, 2026, aligned to CDLAC Round 2; awards May 5, 2026). 2027 term sheet expected January 2027; check CalHFA Key Program Dates page.
layering_notes: Must use CalHFA Conduit Issuer Program for construction bonds and CalHFA Tax-Exempt Permanent Loan (minimum $5M perm loan, 1.15x DSCR). Draws on the $100M enhanced state credit MIP set-aside at CTCAC and the $310M State-funded Mixed Income bond set-aside at CDLAC, so MIP projects compete for bonds outside the geographic pools. Cannot be combined with 9% credits. 3% simple interest, residual receipts (50% of surplus cash), coterminous with perm loan, 1% loan fee. Term sheet is silent on prevailing wage; a 3% subordinate loan may fit the Labor Code 1720(c)(6)(E) below-market-loan exemption if 40% of units are restricted at 80% AMI for 20 years, but confirm with counsel. Governor's reorganization moves MIP into HDFC with HCD programs for a unified application.

program_name: CalHFA Tax-Exempt Permanent Loan Program
administering_agency: California Housing Finance Agency (CalHFA)
typical_award_size: Minimum $5M permanent loan; sized to 1.15x DSCR (max 1.20x year 1 when paired with a CalHFA subsidy loan), lesser of 90% of restricted appraised value or 100% of development cost; combined LTV up to 120% with CalHFA subordinate debt. Rate: 15- or 30-year AAA MMD plus CalHFA spread (estimated 2.20% to 3.75%). Up to 40-year amortization; fully amortizing or 17- or 30-year balloon. Fees: $10,000 application, 1.50% funding fee, $7,500 annual monitoring. HUD/FHA Risk Share credit enhancement.
affordability_requirement: Greater of existing restrictions or 20% at 50% AMI or 40% at 60% AMI (with 10% at 50% AMI); rents at least 10% below market.
next_deadline: Rolling; CalHFA publishes application milestones keyed to each CDLAC round (2026: borrower submittals due Jan 13, April 28, Aug 18 for conduit-only; MIP workbook March 2).
layering_notes: CalHFA must be the bond issuer when it provides the perm loan. Works with or without 4% credits. Required first lien for MIP projects. All other soft financing must be subordinate and coterminous. Term sheet last revised January 2026.

program_name: CalHFA Conduit Issuer Program
administering_agency: California Housing Finance Agency (CalHFA)
typical_award_size: Bond amount set by the lender's loan. Issuer fee: greater of $15,000 or 18.75 bps up to $20M, then $37,500 plus 5 bps above $20M. Annual monitoring 5 bps (minimum $4,000). $5,000 application fee. CDLAC allocation fee 0.035% and 0.50% performance deposit (max $100,000) pass through.
affordability_requirement: 20% at 50% AMI or 40% at 60% AMI (with 10% at 50% AMI); 501(c)(3) bonds require 75% of units at or below 80% AMI. Regulatory agreement for the longer of the qualified project period, bond term, CDLAC resolution term or 55 years.
next_deadline: Rolling; tied to CDLAC rounds (2026 CalHFA conduit-only submittal deadlines Jan 13, April 28, Aug 18).
layering_notes: Statewide alternative to local issuers (CSCDA, CMFA, housing authorities). Mandatory for MIP projects and for CalHFA perm loan projects. Can issue recycled bonds and 501(c)(3) bonds. Term sheet effective for applications after Jan 1, 2023 (last revised Feb 2023).

program_name: CalHFA Bond Recycling Program
administering_agency: California Housing Finance Agency (CalHFA)
typical_award_size: Recycled volume cap subject to availability. For 100% affordable projects, recycled bonds may fund up to 45% of total development cost with CDLAC allocation for the remaining 55%; refinance or market-to-affordable conversions up to 100%; 80/20 projects up to 80%. $25,000 transaction fee plus conduit fees.
affordability_requirement: 20% at 50% AMI or 40% at 60% AMI (with 10% at 50% AMI); 80/20 structure requires 20% of units at or below 60% AMI. Affordability generally 55 years from closing.
next_deadline: Rolling, subject to recycled cap availability.
layering_notes: Recycled bonds cannot generate 4% LIHTC and are excluded from the aggregate basis test, so they reduce the CDLAC allocation a project needs while the CDLAC-allocated portion still generates credits. Must be drawn within 180 days of preservation and issued within four years of the original bonds. Useful for preservation and 80/20 deals that cannot win competitive CDLAC pools. Term sheet last revised April 2022.

program_name: Local Government Special Needs Housing Program (SNHP)
administering_agency: California Housing Finance Agency (CalHFA), with county MHSA funds
typical_award_size: Historically county-funded MHSA capital loans and capitalized operating subsidies administered by CalHFA (16 participating counties as of 2019).
affordability_requirement: Permanent supportive housing units for persons with serious mental illness eligible for MHSA services.
next_deadline: Program discontinued effective January 3, 2020 per DHCS Information Notice 19-047; no new rounds.
layering_notes: No live CalHFA program page exists; the CalHFA multifamily programs page (source) no longer lists SNHP, and a DHCS notice (BH-IN-19-047) states CalHFA discontinued the program effective Jan 3, 2020 with county MHSA funds reverting to county control. Marked needs_confirmation because the DHCS notice could not be opened this pass. Successor supportive housing capital now comes from Homekey+, HCD MHP supportive units, and county Behavioral Health Services Act (Prop 1) housing allocations (research in Pass 2). CTCAC still lists SNHP commitments as qualifying homeless-assistance funding in the nonprofit set-aside.

program_name: Section 811 Project Rental Assistance (PRA)
administering_agency: California Housing Finance Agency (CalHFA) with HCD and DHCS
typical_award_size: $8M HUD award supporting over 600 units statewide; 20-year renewable project-based rental assistance contracts.
affordability_requirement: Units for extremely low-income Medi-Cal beneficiaries with disabilities ages 18 to 61 transitioning from institutions or homeless/at risk. Project must have state agency development financing.
next_deadline: Round IV NOFA closed due to oversubscription; CalHFA is not accepting applications.
layering_notes: Operating subsidy, not capital. Historically layered on CTCAC and HCD-financed projects to support special needs units. Monitor for a future HUD 811 PRA award.

program_name: Multifamily Housing Program (MHP)
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD); transferring to Housing Development and Finance Committee (HDFC) under the California Housing and Homelessness Agency effective July 1, 2026
typical_award_size: 2025 Super NOFA Round 3: $230M MHP of $382M total. 2026 MHP Gap Funding NOFA: $240M, awards $3M to $15M per project, HCD funds capped at 60% of total development cost. Super NOFA per-project cap $50M across MFSN loans, COSR and services reserves; $80M per sponsor per round. Prop 1 (2018) authorized $1.5B for MHP.
per_unit_cap: Base $250,000 per restricted unit (plus $25,000 for emerging developer joint ventures or High/Highest Resource areas; plus $25,000 per Medi-Cal supportive services unit and $100,000 per project for services space). Gap NOFA scored requests up to $250,000 per unit.
affordability_requirement: Restricted units at or below 60% AMI; scoring rewards deeper targeting (30 points for lowest incomes). 55-year regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: No window open as of 2026-11-06. Last round: 2026 MHP Gap Funding NOFA (Round 4) due June 5, 2026, awards August 2026. Next round expected through HDFC's unified multifamily application; timing unannounced.
layering_notes: Core state gap loan: 55-year, 3% simple interest, 0.42% annual payment for 30 years, permanent financing only (construction must not have started at application). Delivered through the Multifamily Finance Super NOFA alongside IIG, VHHP and Joe Serna under AB 434. Pairs with 9% or 4% credits; an MHP award qualifies a project for CDLAC's ELI/VLI set-aside and CTCAC's nonprofit homeless priority. HCD stacking of multiple HCD sources on the same unit allowed within per-unit limits (Admin Notice 21-06). Gap NOFA awardees must apply in the next CDLAC round. HCD loans are public funds; state prevailing wage applies unless a Labor Code 1720(c) exemption fits. MHP can fund capitalized operating subsidy reserves (max $10M per project) and supportive services reserves as grants.

program_name: Multifamily Finance Super NOFA (MFSN) umbrella
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) / Housing Development and Finance Committee (HDFC)
typical_award_size: Round 3 (Feb 13, 2025): $382M (MHP $230M, Joe Serna $120M, IIG $20M, VHHP $12M), applications due April 15, 2025; a separate $96M Disaster Impacted Areas NOFA and a Tribal MFSN. Round 4 (2026 MHP Gap Funding NOFA): $240M for construction-ready projects with an existing HCD award that lack bonds/4% credits, due June 5, 2026.
per_unit_cap: Program-specific: $250,000 base per unit (MHP, SHMHP, TOD), $300,000 (VHHP, Joe Serna), IIG grant table by bedroom and AMI.
affordability_requirement: At or below 60% AMI for assisted units (80% AMI for Joe Serna). 55-year regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: Window closed as of 2026-11-06. Governor's reorganization (effective July 1, 2026) consolidates HCD multifamily programs and CalHFA MIP under HDFC with a single application and unified scoring; next NOFA timing unannounced. Check hcd.ca.gov/funding/supernofa and housing.ca.gov.
layering_notes: One application for MHP, IIG, VHHP, Joe Serna (and SHMHP/TOD when funded). Universal scoring: lowest income levels, state policy priorities, experience, readiness, infill/amenities, cost containment, tiebreaker on public leverage. Awards sized to fill the gap after tax credit equity and permanent debt. Projects then compete at CDLAC/CTCAC; an HCD award unlocks CDLAC ELI/VLI set-aside eligibility. Emerging developer joint applications get a $25,000 per unit bonus. Gap NOFA excluded projects that already closed construction financing.

program_name: Infill Infrastructure Grant Program (IIG-2007 and IIG-2019)
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) / HDFC
typical_award_size: 2025 Super NOFA Round 3: $20M. Qualifying Infill Project grants minimum $1M urban ($500,000 rural), maximum $10M per project under that NOFA. Grant sized by unit count, bedroom mix, affordability and density (net density multiplier up to 1.52 at 105+ units per acre).
per_unit_cap: Per QIP unit table (Round 3): 60% AMI rental $41,000 (0-bdrm) to $71,100 (4-bdrm); 50% AMI $47,400 to $79,000; 30% AMI $55,300 to $90,000; unrestricted units $4,700 to $23,700.
affordability_requirement: Infill projects with affordable units; higher grants for deeper affordability. 55-year affordability covenant recorded against the site.
next_deadline: Closed as of 2026-11-06; last funded in 2025 Super NOFA Round 3 (due April 15, 2025) and included in the 2026 MHP Gap Funding NOFA for projects with prior awards. Next round via HDFC unified NOFA, timing unannounced.
layering_notes: Funds capital improvement projects (infrastructure, factory-built housing components, adaptive reuse) tied to a specific residential or mixed-use infill development, not vertical construction. Stacks on top of MHP or AHSC in the same Super NOFA application and reduces the basis the tax credits must cover. Catalytic Qualifying Infill Area solicitations (for local governments) are closed. Grant is public funds for prevailing wage purposes.

program_name: Veterans Housing and Homelessness Prevention Program (VHHP)
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) with CalVet / HDFC
typical_award_size: Prop 41 (2014) authorized $600M; 2025 Super NOFA Round 3 offered only $12M, indicating the bond authority is nearly exhausted. Loan terms match MHP (55-year, 3% simple, 0.42% payments).
per_unit_cap: $300,000 base per assisted unit (plus $25,000 bonuses available under Super NOFA).
affordability_requirement: Assisted units at or below 60% AMI for veterans and their families; at least 50% of funds must serve extremely low-income veteran households, and 60% of those ELI units must be supportive housing.
next_deadline: Closed as of 2026-11-06; funded through the Super NOFA when dollars remain. Remaining Prop 41 authority not stated on the HCD page; confirm with HCDVets@hcd.ca.gov before underwriting.
layering_notes: Applied for inside the Super NOFA with MHP. Pairs with HUD-VASH vouchers and Homekey+ veteran units; CTCAC counts VHHP capital toward the nonprofit set-aside homeless priority. Veteran definition includes other-than-honorable discharges. Little money left; Homekey+ ($1.03B for veteran PSH) is now the larger state veteran capital source.

program_name: Joe Serna, Jr. Farmworker Housing Grant Program (FWHG)
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) / HDFC
typical_award_size: 2025 Super NOFA Round 3: $120M. Multifamily rental: deferred-payment loans or forgivable-loan grants, including construction financing; loan terms follow MHP.
affordability_requirement: Households deriving 50% or more of income from agricultural employment; units at or below 80% AMI (units above 60% AMI funded at 60% AMI limits). 55-year restrictions.
next_deadline: Closed as of 2026-11-06; next round via HDFC unified NOFA, timing unannounced. Homeownership component funded via the Homeownership Super NOFA.
layering_notes: May be combined with federal and state farmworker tax credits and USDA 514/516. Proposed CTCAC 2027 rules would route the $25M enhanced farmworker state credits through Serna awards beginning 2028. Relevant for Napa, Sonoma, Yolo, Solano and San Joaquin projects. Only HCD program allowing construction-period financing.

program_name: Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Implementation Program
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) / HDFC
typical_award_size: Historically loans and grants for higher-density affordable housing and related infrastructure near transit; 2025 Super NOFA listed TOD with $250,000 base per unit loans. AB 130 (2025) refocuses the program on affordable housing funded by a state vehicle miles traveled mitigation bank.
per_unit_cap: $250,000 base per assisted unit (2025 Super NOFA terms).
affordability_requirement: Assisted units at or below 60% AMI; 55-year restrictions.
next_deadline: Application window listed as PENDING; 2026 TOD Guidelines posted. No NOFA date announced as of 2026-11-06.
layering_notes: Overlaps with AHSC for transit-adjacent sites; AHSC has far more money. Watch for a VMT mitigation bank funded round in 2027. Eligible applicants include cities, counties, transit agencies and developers.

program_name: Housing for a Healthy California (HHC)
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD)
typical_award_size: Article I (developers, federal NHTF funds): capital loans and operating reserve grants; 2020-21 NOFA about $160M. Article II (counties, SB 2 funds). No funding available since the 2021 Article I round.
affordability_requirement: Supportive housing for Medi-Cal eligible chronically homeless or high-cost health users; extremely low income.
next_deadline: Archived program; no funding available (HCD 2025 Super NOFA footnote). No new rounds expected.
layering_notes: Historically paired with NHTF and MHP for PSH. CTCAC still recognizes HHC commitments in the nonprofit set-aside homeless priority for existing awards. Successor PSH capital: Homekey+, MHP COSR grants.

program_name: Portfolio Reinvestment Program (PRP)
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD)
typical_award_size: Rehabilitation loans up to $25M at 30- to 55-year terms, 3% simple interest, 0.42% annual payments, plus forgivable capitalized operating subsidy reserve loans up to 25% of the rehab loan. 2022 NOFA about $332.5M; Round 2 NOFA Dec 28, 2023. Set-asides: $10M small projects (20 units or fewer), $25M residential hotels, $25M foreclosed projects.
affordability_requirement: Existing HCD-funded projects with 5 or more units whose HCD restrictions expire by Dec 31, 2033, legacy-program projects without recent rehab, or foreclosed projects; affordability extended.
next_deadline: Application window closed; no new round announced as of 2026-11-06. Contact portfolioreinvestment@hcd.ca.gov for eligibility list.
layering_notes: Only for HCD portfolio projects (expansion list published by HCD). Pairs with 4% resyndication and CDLAC Acquisition/Rehabilitation pool. Not a source for new developments.

program_name: Homekey+
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) with CalVet
typical_award_size: Approximately $2.145B (Prop 1 Behavioral Health Infrastructure Bond plus HHAP supplemental): $1.033B for veteran-serving PSH, $1.11B for other target populations. Baseline $200,000 per door (acquisition plus rehab or new construction), plus up to $100,000 per door with 1:1 local capital match (1:2 for veteran units, i.e., $50,000 match earns $100,000). Operating grants per door also available with match. Awards as of July 2, 2026 listed on the HCD awardee list; March 2026 awards totaled $131.8M for eight projects.
per_unit_cap: $200,000 per door baseline; up to $300,000 per door with match; new construction cost containment caps raised March 27, 2026
affordability_requirement: Permanent supportive housing for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness with a behavioral health challenge; veteran and youth allocations. Applicants must coordinate with county behavioral health departments.
next_deadline: Over the counter until funds are exhausted (NOFA amended March 27, 2026). Applications after Aug 7, 2025 prioritized by veteran units; unrequested regional allocations moved to a discretionary reserve Oct 8, 2025. Pre-application consultation required via HCD Connect.
layering_notes: Eligible applicants are cities, counties, tribes and public entities, with developers as co-applicants (an LP may be co-applicant). March 2026 amendments allow projects with pending or future CTCAC/CDLAC applications (six months to secure awards), HCD portfolio projects with expiring regulatory agreements adding veteran units, and gap funding for stalled projects. Stacks with 4% credits, MHP and local funds; Homekey funding counts toward CTCAC homeless priority. NOFA Section 509 requires certification of state prevailing wage compliance or exemption under Gov. Code 65913.4(a)(9); statutory CEQA exemption available. Tribal Homekey+ ($121M) is separate.

program_name: Homekey (Rounds 1 through 3)
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD)
typical_award_size: About $3.57B over three rounds; Round 3 (FY 2022-23) about $736M. 15,962 homes and 261 projects funded as of Sept 15, 2026.
affordability_requirement: Permanent or interim housing for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness.
next_deadline: No longer accepting applications; HCD directs applicants to Homekey+.
layering_notes: Legacy program. Existing Homekey sites can seek Homekey+ or MHP gap funds and qualify as adaptive reuse under CTCAC definitions. Local public entity applicants with developer partners.

program_name: No Place Like Home (NPLH)
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD)
typical_award_size: Up to $2B in Prop 2 (2018) revenue bonds for county-sponsored PSH; county noncompetitive allocations plus competitive rounds (Round 4 last).
affordability_requirement: Permanent supportive housing for people with serious mental illness who are homeless, chronically homeless or at risk.
next_deadline: No longer accepting applications; no future rounds stated. Counties (and City of Berkeley) were the applicants.
layering_notes: Counties in scope may still hold uncommitted NPLH allocations or returned funds; check in Pass 2 (Sacramento, Alameda, Contra Costa had large allocations). NPLH commitments count toward CTCAC nonprofit set-aside homeless priority and CDLAC ELI/VLI set-aside eligibility. Successor: Homekey+ and county BHSA housing funds.

program_name: Supportive Housing Multifamily Housing Program (SHMHP)
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD)
typical_award_size: 55-year loans at 3% simple interest with 0.42% annual payments (2018 NOFA); $250,000 base per unit when offered through the Super NOFA.
per_unit_cap: $250,000 base per assisted unit (2025 Super NOFA terms)
affordability_requirement: Minimum of 5 supportive housing units or 40% of total units, whichever is greater; assisted units at or below 60% AMI.
next_deadline: Archived; last NOFA 2018. Residual funds were folded into the 2025 Super NOFA Disaster Impacted Areas NOFA.
layering_notes: Functionally replaced by MHP supportive housing provisions (AB 2483, SB 482) and Homekey+.

program_name: National Housing Trust Fund (NHTF), state allocation
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD)
typical_award_size: Annual federal allocation (varies); deferred-payment or forgivable loans. Most recent: 2024-25 Project Solicitation (amended) with awards posted.
affordability_requirement: Extremely low-income households (30% AMI); 55-year regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: Closed as of 2026-11-06; a 2025-26 or 2026-27 solicitation has not been posted. Monitor the HCD NHTF page.
layering_notes: Federal NHTF itself does not carry Davis-Bacon, but the HCD loan is state public funds, so state prevailing wage applies. Pairs with 9% credits for deep ELI targeting; HCD has historically run NHTF through HHC Article I and stand-alone solicitations rather than the Super NOFA.

program_name: California Housing Accelerator
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD)
typical_award_size: $1.75B (ARPA, 2021-22 budget); 58 projects and 4,945 units funded. Forgivable 0% loans for 20 years filling the full permanent gap for shovel-ready HCD-funded projects that could not obtain bonds or 4% credits.
affordability_requirement: Per underlying HCD program award.
next_deadline: Closed (Tier 2 applications due April 8, 2022; permanent loan conversion deadline Nov 30, 2026). No new rounds; the 2026 MHP Gap Funding NOFA plays a similar role.
layering_notes: Historical reference only. Shows HCD's pattern of periodic gap rounds for stalled awarded projects (Accelerator 2021-22, MHP Gap NOFA 2026).

program_name: Local Housing Trust Fund (LHTF) Program
administering_agency: California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD)
typical_award_size: Dollar-for-dollar matching grants to local and regional housing trust funds (public, joint public-private or 501(c)(3)); 2024 Round 5 was the last NOFA. Trust funds then lend to projects.
affordability_requirement: At least 30% of each allocation for extremely low-income households; no more than 20% for moderate income; 55-year rental restrictions.
next_deadline: No longer accepting applications; Round 5 (2024) closed. Future rounds depend on state budget.
layering_notes: Developers access LHTF money through local trust funds (e.g., Sacramento Housing Trust Fund, Napa, Sonoma, Yolo, Marin trust funds, Bay Area Housing Finance Authority), which should be captured in Pass 2 and 3. State match funds are public funds for prevailing wage.

program_name: Golden State Acquisition Fund (GSAF)
administering_agency: HCD seed capital; administered by Corporation for Supportive Housing and partner CDFIs (fund managers)
typical_award_size: Short-term acquisition and predevelopment loans from a revolving fund seeded by HCD and leveraged with private capital; terms set by fund managers.
affordability_requirement: Sites to be developed or preserved as affordable housing; terms per fund manager.
next_deadline: Rolling through fund managers listed at goldenstate-fund.com.
layering_notes: Listed on HCD's grants and funding page with an external link; the fund's own site was not opened this pass, so terms need confirmation. Bridge financing only; repaid at construction closing from LIHTC/bond sources.

program_name: Affordable Housing and Sustainable Communities (AHSC)
administering_agency: Strategic Growth Council (SGC) with HCD implementing
typical_award_size: Round 10 NOFA (March 4, 2026): approximately $750M (20% of Cap-and-Invest auction proceeds through 2030). Per project $10M minimum, $50M maximum; AHD loans plus HRI grants must be at least 50% of the request and no more than $35M; STI/PGM grants up to $15M; $100M per recipient per round.
per_unit_cap: Rental AHD loans: $250,000 base per assisted unit (inclusive of prior HCD loans). HRI grants $35,000 per residential unit or $50,000 per restricted unit.
affordability_requirement: At least 20% of AHD units affordable; rental AHDs must average 60% AMI or below across restricted units; 55-year covenant. Density minimums (TOD 30 units/acre or FAR 2.0; ICP lower; RIPA lowest). Three project area types: Transit Oriented Development, Integrated Connectivity Project, Rural Innovation Project Area.
next_deadline: Round 10 closed May 4, 2026; awards to be adopted at the Dec 16, 2026 Council meeting. Round 11 guidelines expected late 2026 or early 2027 with a spring 2027 application deadline (Round 10 pattern: draft guidelines Dec 19, NOFA March 4, due May 4).
layering_notes: Joint application by the developer and a public agency (city, county or transit agency) covering housing (AHD loan), housing-related infrastructure, sustainable transportation infrastructure and programs. AHD loan terms follow MHP (55-year, 3% simple, residual receipts). Guidelines state AHSC funds are public funding subject to the State Prevailing Wage Law. Concurrent 4% AHSC and 9% CTCAC applications prohibited; one switch between 4% and 9% allowed. An AHSC award qualifies the project for the CDLAC ELI/VLI set-aside. Commonly stacked: 4% credits + CDLAC bonds + AHSC + MIP or MHP + local funds. Also stacks with IIG (both infrastructure), but HCD stacking limits apply across AHD and HRI funds. West Sacramento and Sacramento projects have been frequent winners.

program_name: Transformative Climate Communities (TCC) Round 6
administering_agency: Strategic Growth Council (SGC)
typical_award_size: Round 6 funded by Prop 4 (2024 Climate Bond); amount not stated on the program page. Implementation grants for place-based plans in disadvantaged communities that can include affordable housing capital as one project component.
affordability_requirement: Housing components must be affordable per TCC guidelines; project must sit within a TCC-eligible disadvantaged community boundary.
next_deadline: Round 6 applications closed Sept 30, 2026 (implementation pre-proposals June 30, 2026); awards expected Spring 2027. Future rounds depend on Prop 4 appropriations.
layering_notes: Community-led collaborative applications (lead applicant typically a city or county) rather than developer-driven. Past awards included Stockton and Sacramento area communities, so San Joaquin and Sacramento sites may qualify. Housing funds within TCC follow AHSC-like terms; state grant funds are generally public funds for prevailing wage, verify in Round 6 guidelines.

program_name: Welfare Exemption from Property Tax for Low-Income Rental Housing
administering_agency: State Board of Equalization (BOE) issues Organizational and Supplemental Clearance Certificates; county assessors grant the exemption
typical_award_size: Full exemption of property tax on qualifying low-income units (partial exemption proportional to qualifying units); typically worth 1% to 1.25% of assessed value annually. Non-LIHTC, non-government-financed properties owned by nonprofits or eligible LLCs are limited to $20,000,000 of exempt assessed value statewide per claimant.
affordability_requirement: Units occupied by lower-income households (80% AMI or below, with the 140% over-income continuation rule) under a recorded regulatory agreement or LIHTC. Limited partnership owners qualify only if the managing general partner is an eligible nonprofit or LLC holding an OCC and the property has LIHTC or government financing.
next_deadline: Annual claim due to the county assessor between January 1 and 5:00 p.m. February 15 (next: Feb 15, 2027); late claims receive 85% to 90% of the exemption. First-time claimants must obtain a BOE Organizational Clearance Certificate (Form BOE-277) and, for limited partnerships, a Supplemental Clearance Certificate (Form BOE-277-L1, wet signature) before the assessor can grant the exemption.
layering_notes: Standard component of every LIHTC underwriting: nonprofit managing GP structure is required for the exemption, which in turn supports debt sizing on 4% and 9% deals. Also applies to supportive housing and welfare-exempt nonprofit-owned projects without LIHTC up to the $20M cap. County assessors in all 12 target counties administer claims (forms BOE-267, 267-L, 267-L1); construction-period exemption available once an OCC is in place and the property is under development for exempt use. Property tax exemption does not affect prevailing wage.

program_name: SHRA Multifamily Lending Program (County gap financing)
administering_agency: Sacramento Housing and Redevelopment Agency (SHRA) on behalf of the County of Sacramento and the Housing Authority of the County of Sacramento
typical_award_size: Gap loans sized to the financing gap after all other sources; no stated per-project cap. County funds posted June 1, 2026: HOME $2,500,000, Housing Trust Fund $900,000, Affordable Housing Ordinance fund $6,000,000, PLHA $0 (total about $9.4M). Recent County commitments: San Juan Phase II $11.7M (HOME $7.0M plus PLHA $4.7M, 70 units), Shiloh Arms $2.12M HOME, South Sacramento Homekey $1.9M. Projects must have 12 or more units.
per_unit_cap: None published; HOME-assisted units capped by 24 CFR 92.250 maximum per-unit subsidy. SHRA charges $100 per SHRA-funded unit per year.
affordability_requirement: 55-year regulatory agreement. Minimum per source: HOME 20% of HOME units at 50% AMI and the rest at or below 60% AMI; AHO fund 20% at 50% AMI and 80% at 60% AMI; Housing Trust Fund 50% to 80% AMI workforce households. Priorities: preservation at risk, then new construction (PSH and homeless, veterans, workforce 30% to 60% AMI, other), then rehab. Deeper affordability preferred.
next_deadline: Two rounds a year aligned to CTCAC 9% rounds; 2026 pre-application deadlines were Jan 2 and July 1, 2026 with full applications March 2 and Sept 1 (Board/Council approvals June 16, 2026 and Jan 19, 2027). SHRA was not accepting pre-applications as of 2026-11-06; the 2027 schedule and funds-available notice are expected on the SHRA multifamily page about 30 days before the next pre-application deadline (likely early January 2027). Pre-applications go through Builder's Patch.
layering_notes: This is the primary local soft source for 9% and 4% deals in the unincorporated county (City of Sacramento projects use the parallel City pool, Pass 3). Terms: up to 4% simple interest, term up to 40 years from conversion or 55 years when senior public lenders require, 1.10x to 1.20x combined DSCR, 90% combined LTV, payments deferred during construction and deferred developer fee then amortized, residual receipts only when state or federal lenders require it. Nonprofit managing general partner required; applicants need prior affordable housing ownership experience. $12,500 good-faith deposit at full application; annual administration fee 12.5 bps of loan (max $15,000) or 5 bps of bonds (min $15,000). SHRA issues the CTCAC local needs letter and conduit bonds (see separate bond record). Applicants request gap funds without specifying a source; SHRA picks the source, so Davis-Bacon exposure depends on whether HOME (12+ units) or CDBG (8+ units) is assigned, and state prevailing wage applies unless the below-market-loan exemption (40% of units at 80% AMI for 20 years) fits. Pre-applications are timed so SHRA commitments are in hand before CTCAC and CDLAC deadlines, satisfying CDLAC readiness and the CTCAC tiebreaker. SB 802 (Chapter 417, Statutes of 2026) requires the County and cities to form the Sacramento Area Housing and Homelessness Agency, a regional JPA that absorbs SHRA, by January 1, 2028; expect program administration, fee funds and NOFA calendars to migrate to that agency during 2027-2028.

program_name: Sacramento County Affordable Housing Ordinance Fund (AHO affordability fee)
administering_agency: County of Sacramento (Planning and Environmental Review collects fee); SHRA administers the fund and lends it through the Multifamily Lending Program
typical_award_size: $6,000,000 available for new County projects as of June 1, 2026. 2024 fee revenue $5,128,243; year-end 2024 balance $11.1M ($6.3M uncommitted). 2014 to 2024 cumulative $32.8M, funding eight projects (650 units); AHO money averaged about 9% of total development cost and reached 61% of new affordable units built in the unincorporated area. Typical commitments $400,000 to $6.4M per project (Cornerstone South $6.43M for 29 AHO units; San Juan $5.2M for 21 units; Beech Hill $2.47M for 11 units).
per_unit_cap: None published; recent awards ranged roughly $200,000 to $250,000 per AHO-restricted unit.
affordability_requirement: Fund-assisted units: 20% at 50% AMI and 80% at 60% AMI, workforce (labor force) households, 55 years. At least 10% of fees must buy down units to extremely low income (30% AMI); at least 50% of fees must produce housing within large (750+ unit) development projects, which steers money to the Vineyard, North Vineyard Station, Florin Vineyard and similar growth areas.
next_deadline: Awarded only through SHRA's twice-yearly multifamily pre-application rounds (next expected January 2027). Fee side: $3.91 per habitable square foot of market-rate unit as of March 27, 2026, adjusted each spring by the ENR building cost index.
layering_notes: Unincorporated-county-only money (fee is charged only on unincorporated residential permits). Normally paired with 4% credits plus bonds or 9% credits, SHRA HOME, PLHA and the County Housing Trust Fund in one SHRA award. Developer side of the ordinance: market-rate projects may instead dedicate land, build units, enter a development agreement with an Affordable Housing Strategy, or buy banked unit credits from SHRA; multifamily projects with at least 20% affordable units at 17 or more units per acre are exempt from the fee, which is itself a meaningful incentive for mixed-income rental. AHO is a local below-market loan, so the Labor Code 1720(c)(6)(E) exemption may apply if no HOME or CDBG is in the stack; confirm with counsel. The County is mid-way through an AHO amendment study (Housing Element Program E3): KMA found 2% to 14% affordable production versus the 10% target; Board workshop Oct 6, 2026, nexus study through spring 2027, ordinance hearings expected winter 2027, possibly adding an inclusionary option and resource-area targeting. SB 802 (Chapter 417, Statutes of 2026) requires the County and cities to form the Sacramento Area Housing and Homelessness Agency, a regional JPA that absorbs SHRA, by January 1, 2028; expect program administration, fee funds and NOFA calendars to migrate to that agency during 2027-2028.

program_name: Sacramento County Housing Trust Fund (commercial linkage fee)
administering_agency: County of Sacramento (Chapter 16.89, fee collected at building permit); SHRA administers and lends the fund
typical_award_size: $900,000 available as of June 1, 2026 (was $0 in June 2025). 2024 fee revenue $1,605,084; year-end 2024 balance $6.36M ($1.2M uncommitted). Since 1991: $33.1M in fees, 29 developments, 3,037 total units. Recent loans $816,000 to $5.25M per project (San Juan $5.25M for 21 HTF units; Terracina at Wildhawk $4.6M for 18 units).
per_unit_cap: None published; recent awards about $250,000 per HTF-restricted unit.
affordability_requirement: Households at 50% to 80% of county AMI who are in the labor force (jobs-housing linkage); 55-year regulatory agreement.
next_deadline: Through SHRA multifamily pre-application rounds (next expected January 2027). Current fee schedule (2024 report): office and hotel $3.26, research and development and commercial $2.17, manufacturing and warehouse $1.08 per gross square foot, adjusted annually.
layering_notes: Oldest local source (1990). Revenue tracks commercial construction and is volatile, so the balance is usually smaller than the AHO fund. Used mainly for new construction workforce units at 50% to 80% AMI, which complements deeper-targeted HOME or MHP units in the same project. Local below-market loan; state prevailing wage exemption may be available absent federal funds. The companion City of Sacramento Housing Trust Fund (City Code 18.56) is a separate pool covered in Pass 3. SB 802 (Chapter 417, Statutes of 2026) requires the County and cities to form the Sacramento Area Housing and Homelessness Agency, a regional JPA that absorbs SHRA, by January 1, 2028; expect program administration, fee funds and NOFA calendars to migrate to that agency during 2027-2028.

program_name: HOME Investment Partnerships Program, Sacramento County HOME Consortium
administering_agency: SHRA for the County of Sacramento (lead entity) and consortium cities Citrus Heights, Folsom, Rancho Cordova, Galt and Isleton
typical_award_size: 2027 Action Plan: $2,825,253 annual allocation plus $900,000 program income ($3.73M total). 2024 entitlement $2,965,817; year-end 2024 balance $15.7M ($9.1M uncommitted). $2,500,000 posted as available June 1, 2026. Recent project loans $1.5M to $8.9M (Arden Star $8.9M for 48 HOME units; Madison Square $4.45M; San Juan Phase II $4.2M).
per_unit_cap: HUD 221(d)(3) per-unit subsidy limits under 24 CFR 92.250; recent awards roughly $170,000 to $210,000 per HOME unit.
affordability_requirement: 20% of HOME-assisted units at 50% AMI (Low HOME rents), remainder at or below 60% AMI with rents at 65% AMI; federal affordability period 5 to 20 years but SHRA records 55-year restrictions. 15% CHDO set-aside.
next_deadline: Through SHRA multifamily pre-application rounds (next expected January 2027); HUD program year is the calendar year, 2027 Action Plan drafted August 2026.
layering_notes: Applies to the unincorporated county and the five consortium cities (Elk Grove and the City of Sacramento are separate HUD entitlements). HOME on 12 or more units triggers Davis-Bacon, and SHRA policy requires the higher of state or federal wage by trade when both apply; applicants must flag wage assumptions in the SHRA narrative. HOME units stack with CTCAC units but the HOME rent and income rules are the binding constraint on those units. SHRA may assign HOME rather than local fee funds to a request, so underwrite wages conservatively. Environmental review (NEPA) deadline falls two months after SHRA's application deadline. SB 802 (Chapter 417, Statutes of 2026) requires the County and cities to form the Sacramento Area Housing and Homelessness Agency, a regional JPA that absorbs SHRA, by January 1, 2028; expect program administration, fee funds and NOFA calendars to migrate to that agency during 2027-2028.

program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG), Urban County of Sacramento
administering_agency: SHRA for the County of Sacramento
typical_award_size: 2027 Action Plan: $6,151,763 allocation plus $2,025,000 prior-year resources ($8.18M); about $3.63M targeted to the housing development, preservation and homeownership goal (27 rental units rehabilitated, 10 constructed, 100 owner rehabs), the rest to infrastructure and public services. June 2025 notice listed $0 County CDBG for multifamily; June 2026 notice did not list CDBG.
affordability_requirement: At least 51% of assisted units for households at or below 80% AMI.
next_deadline: Through SHRA rounds when offered (rehabilitation projects only); 2027 program year begins January 2027.
layering_notes: Limited developer value: CDBG cannot fund new construction unless carried out by a Community Based Development Organization, and SHRA offers it only for rehabilitation. Davis-Bacon applies at 8 or more units. Useful for acquisition-rehab or preservation deals paired with 4% credits and CalHFA or SHRA bonds. CDBG-CV balances are committed to the Mather Community Campus shelter.

program_name: Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA), County of Sacramento
administering_agency: County of Sacramento (HCD entitlement recipient); SHRA administers the multifamily share
typical_award_size: 2024 PLHA income $6,666,613; year-end 2024 uncommitted multifamily balance $2,245,525 and single-family (down payment assistance) balance $2,804,135. Recent multifamily commitments: Arden Star $2.42M (13 units), San Juan $1.7M (7 units), San Juan Phase II $2.7M then increased to $4.7M (70 units). $0 posted as available for County projects June 1, 2026.
per_unit_cap: None published; recent awards about $185,000 to $245,000 per PLHA unit.
affordability_requirement: Multifamily share for households at or below 60% AMI (with workforce flexibility under the County's PLHA plan); 55-year restriction. At least 25% of each allocation is reserved for down payment assistance below 50% AMI.
next_deadline: Through SHRA multifamily rounds as annual HCD PLHA disbursements arrive (SB 2 recording-fee revenue, variable). Next SHRA round expected January 2027; check the funds-available notice for a PLHA line.
layering_notes: State formula money without federal strings, so it is the preferred SHRA source when Davis-Bacon must be avoided (state prevailing wage still applies unless the below-market-loan exemption is met). Often paired with HOME in the same SHRA award (San Juan Phase II). The separate HCD Local Housing Trust Fund match program is no longer funding; the County's last LHTF award was 2024. SB 802 negotiations included language keeping PLHA flowing to all jurisdictions once the regional agency forms. SB 802 (Chapter 417, Statutes of 2026) requires the County and cities to form the Sacramento Area Housing and Homelessness Agency, a regional JPA that absorbs SHRA, by January 1, 2028; expect program administration, fee funds and NOFA calendars to migrate to that agency during 2027-2028.

program_name: SHRA Multifamily Mortgage Revenue Bonds (Housing Authority of the County of Sacramento conduit issuance)
administering_agency: Housing Authority of the County of Sacramento, staffed by SHRA
typical_award_size: No minimum or maximum bond amount; sized to the senior lender's loan. Issuance fee 25 bps of the bond amount at closing; annual administration fee 5 bps of outstanding bonds (minimum $15,000) plus $100 per SHRA-regulated non-bond unit per year; when another issuer is used SHRA still charges up to 0.25% for TEFRA review. CDLAC fees and 0.5% performance deposit pass through.
affordability_requirement: Federal and state minimum: 20% of units at 50% AMI, or 30% at 60% AMI plus 10% at 50% AMI (H&S Code 34312.3); non-competitive CTCAC projects targeting above 60% AMI must average no more than 59% AMI. Rents capped at 30% of 50% or 60% AMI. Bond regulatory agreement for the qualified project period or 55 years from 50% occupancy, incorporating the CDLAC resolution.
next_deadline: Pre-application and full application on the SHRA schedule tied to CDLAC rounds (2026: applications March 2 and Sept 1 for the July/Sept and March/May 2027 CDLAC rounds). Inducement resolution and TEFRA hearing go to the Board of Supervisors or City Council before the CDLAC filing.
layering_notes: Local alternative to CalHFA, CSCDA and CMFA for 4% deals in the City and unincorporated county (other cities by cooperation agreement). SHRA requires projects using other issuers to meet SHRA affordability and due diligence standards and pays for TEFRA review. Nonprofit owners seeking the welfare exemption must show ongoing day-to-day involvement (services, management or maintenance) under SHRA policy 9.1.11. Bonds alone are generally not treated as public funds for state prevailing wage, but SHRA gap loans or HOME in the same deal usually are. Private placements waive the investment-grade rating requirement. SB 802 (Chapter 417, Statutes of 2026) requires the County and cities to form the Sacramento Area Housing and Homelessness Agency, a regional JPA that absorbs SHRA, by January 1, 2028; expect program administration, fee funds and NOFA calendars to migrate to that agency during 2027-2028.

program_name: Project-Based Vouchers, Housing Authority of the County of Sacramento
administering_agency: SHRA (the County housing authority administers all vouchers for both the City and County)
typical_award_size: Competitive RFP awards from the tenant-based HCV allocation or HUD-VASH; no RFP anticipated in 2026. Cap of 25 units or 25% of a building, whichever is greater, with exceptions for elderly or disabled households and units with qualifying supportive services (common for PSH). HAP contract up to 20 years with extensions to 40 years total.
per_unit_cap: 25 units or 25% of units per project unless the supportive-services or elderly/disabled exception applies
affordability_requirement: HCV income limits (very low income, 75% of admissions at or below 30% AMI); PBV units leased through the Coordinated Access System for homeless set-aside units under a Housing First model.
next_deadline: SHRA states it does not anticipate a Project-Based Voucher RFP in 2026; updates come through the SHRA listserv. HUD's 2026 budget guidance also asked PHAs to pause new PBV commitments except for public housing repositioning, so a 2027 RFP is uncertain. Non-competitive PBV remains possible for SHRA-controlled sites and for adding units to existing HAP contracts.
layering_notes: PBV HAP contracts underwrite debt on PSH units (rents at the payment standard, up to 120% of FMR with approval) and were the operating engine for Homekey, NPLH and MHP supportive units in Sacramento. With no 2026 RFP, new PSH deals should plan on Homekey+ operating grants, BHSA rental subsidies or the County Flexible Housing Pool instead. Referral mechanics for PBV PSH run through Sacramento Steps Forward (see Continuum of Care record). SB 802 (Chapter 417, Statutes of 2026) requires the County and cities to form the Sacramento Area Housing and Homelessness Agency, a regional JPA that absorbs SHRA, by January 1, 2028; expect program administration, fee funds and NOFA calendars to migrate to that agency during 2027-2028.

program_name: Sacramento County Affordable Housing Fee Deferral and Waiver Program (county impact fees and SacSewer impact fees)
administering_agency: County of Sacramento Department of Finance with SHRA certification; Sacramento Area Sewer District (SacSewer, formerly SASD and Regional San) for sewer impact fee waivers
typical_award_size: Deferral or waiver of county development impact fees (Antelope, North Vineyard Station, Vineyard and Florin Vineyard plan area fees, library facilities fees, county transportation development fees) and SASD/Regional San sewer impact fees. Waivers are proportional to the share of very low-income units. Annual cap on waivers: greater of 200 dwelling units or 5% of prior-year new residential permits in the unincorporated county. SacSewer reported over $900,000 waived across five projects as of October 2025. $1,000 application fee; deferrals require a 10% fee deposit.
affordability_requirement: Deferral: at least 10% of units affordable to very low income (50% AMI) or 49% affordable to low income (80% AMI). Waiver: at least 10% of units at or below 50% AMI. Fees become due with interest penalties if the units are not delivered within 24 months.
next_deadline: Rolling, before building permit issuance; requires an SHRA Certification Letter, preliminary title report, and a recorded agreement, note and deed of trust (subordinable to construction financing). Deferred fees are due at close of escrow or 24 months after the agreement, whichever is first.
layering_notes: County impact fee relief applies to unincorporated projects; SASD and Regional San sewer impact fee waivers are available in all cities in the county and the unincorporated area. Sewer impact fees in Sacramento run several thousand dollars per unit, so the waiver is worth roughly $5,000 to $10,000 per very-low-income unit; it reduces basis and improves the CTCAC cost-containment score. Labor Code 1720(b)(4) treats fees waived or forgiven by a public agency as public funds, so a waiver can itself trigger state prevailing wage unless the project is otherwise exempt; confirm with counsel. City of Sacramento has its own fee deferral and fee reduction program (Pass 3).

program_name: Sacramento County Affordable Housing Incentive Program (density bonus, Zoning Code Section 6.5.4)
administering_agency: Sacramento County Planning and Environmental Review
typical_award_size: State Density Bonus Law as implemented in the County Zoning Code: 20% bonus for 5% very low income rising to 50% at 15%; 20% for 10% low income rising to 50% at 20%; 80% bonus for 100% affordable projects (up to 20% moderate) plus a three-story or 33-foot height increase within a half mile of a major transit stop; separate schedules for senior, special needs, moderate-income for-sale and land donation. Up to five concessions (one for 5% VLI, three at 15% VLI, four at 16% to 99%, five for 100% affordable; one more for child care). Table 6.4.1 (added June 11, 2026) adds bonus for projects at or below 50% restricted units.
affordability_requirement: Minimum five units with 5% very low, 10% low, 10% moderate (for-sale), or special population set-asides; rental target units restricted 55 years with professional management; units built concurrently and dispersed on site.
next_deadline: Rolling; filed with the entitlement application together with an Affordable Housing Strategies Memorandum; the County does not charge a processing fee for eligible applications (Housing Element page). Affordable Housing Agreement must be recorded before grading and building permits.
layering_notes: Parking maximums: 1 space studio and 1-bedroom, 1.5 for 2- and 3-bedroom, 2.5 for 4-bedroom; within a half mile of major transit 0.5 per bedroom, 0.5 per unit for 100% lower-income rental, none for special needs housing. Waivers of standards that physically preclude the project are unlimited but do not count as concessions. Land donation (one acre or 40 units, zoned 30+ units per acre) earns bonus and can satisfy the AHO. Combine with the AHO fee exemption (20% affordable at 17+ du/ac) and the Countywide Rezone Program sites for by-right or streamlined approval. 100% affordable LIHTC projects typically use the 80% bonus and parking reductions to cut costs rather than add units.

program_name: Welfare Exemption processing, Sacramento County Assessor
administering_agency: Sacramento County Assessor, Institutional Exemptions Section (BOE issues the Organizational Clearance Certificate)
typical_award_size: Exemption of the qualifying low-income share of assessed value from the roughly 1.1% to 1.2% total property tax rate in Sacramento County (plus any direct levies that remain). Annual filing with the Assessor.
affordability_requirement: Per state law: lower-income units (80% AMI, 140% continuation rule) under LIHTC or a recorded regulatory agreement; limited partnerships need a nonprofit or eligible LLC managing general partner with an OCC and a Supplemental Clearance Certificate.
next_deadline: Annual claims due February 15 (next Feb 15, 2027; postmark next business day if a weekend or holiday). First-time filers submit BOE-267 with the BOE-277 OCC and the low-income supplemental affidavit (BOE-267-L or 267-L1 for partnerships). Contact (916) 875-0720 or ASR-InstitutionalExemptions@saccounty.gov.
layering_notes: Sacramento assessor applies the statewide rules (see Pass 1 BOE record); no county-specific abatement JPA exists. SHRA bond policy 9.1.11 additionally requires the nonprofit owner to have material day-to-day involvement (services, management or maintenance) for bond-financed projects claiming the exemption, which aligns with BOE managing-GP scrutiny. File the construction-period claim as soon as the OCC is issued and the site is under development to avoid a year of taxes.

program_name: Sacramento County Behavioral Health (MHSA/BHSA) housing capital for permanent supportive housing
administering_agency: Sacramento County Department of Health Services, Behavioral Health Services, with SHRA screening projects through its multifamily rounds
typical_award_size: Not published. SHRA's June 2025 funds notice stated projects may also be considered for County Behavioral Health MHSA housing program financing for PSH units serving homeless adults with serious mental illness; the 2022-23 MHSA plan dedicated $11M of Community Services and Supports funds to the MHSA Housing Program (secondary source). Recent example: $2.5M MHSA to Auburn Oaks PSH (Hope Cooperative, with SHRA). Beginning July 1, 2026 the Behavioral Health Services Act requires 30% of county BHSA funds for housing interventions, half of that for chronically homeless people, with up to 25% of housing dollars allowed for capital development.
affordability_requirement: PSH units restricted to persons with serious mental illness or substance use disorder who are homeless or at risk, referred through County Behavioral Health; typically 30% AMI or below with rental or operating subsidy.
next_deadline: No stand-alone capital NOFA found as of 2026-11-06; requests ride on SHRA multifamily pre-applications (next expected January 2027). County BHSA Integrated Plan covers July 2026 to June 2029 and is the document to watch for a housing capital line; the County is also procuring a Flexible Housing Pool administrator for BHSA rental subsidies.
layering_notes: Successor to the CalHFA Special Needs Housing Program and county NPLH allocations (NPLH is closed; Sacramento County ran its last Request to Partner in 2020). BHSA capital and operating subsidies can underwrite PSH units in 4% and 9% deals and satisfy CTCAC's nonprofit set-aside homeless priority (MHSA listed as qualifying capital) and the CDLAC Homeless set-aside. Pair with Homekey+ (county received one award in 2025) and HHAP. County funds are public funds for prevailing wage. Amounts and application process should be confirmed with Behavioral Health Services and SHRA before underwriting.

program_name: Sacramento Continuum of Care (CA-503) funding and PBV PSH referral system
administering_agency: Sacramento Steps Forward (CoC lead agency and HMIS lead) for the City and County of Sacramento
typical_award_size: HUD CoC Program awards described as tens of millions per round across more than 30 renewal projects; competition now runs every other year. 2026 competition: local letters of intent for new projects due July 2, 2026, local applications July 14, 2026, consolidated application to HUD Sept 30, 2026. Youth Homelessness Demonstration Program total $8,082,381 across seven projects (as of 2025).
affordability_requirement: CoC PSH serves households experiencing homelessness (chronic homelessness priority) through the Coordinated Access System; rental assistance and leasing, not capital.
next_deadline: 2026 round closed (HUD submission Sept 30, 2026). Next local competition expected 2028 under the every-other-year cycle, with renewals in between.
layering_notes: CoC dollars rarely fund capital, but CoC PSH rental assistance or leasing can replace PBV as the operating subsidy on a share of units, and CoC participation is required for Homekey+ and HHAP coordination. For PBV PSH buildings, SSF runs the lease-up: referrals begin 120 days before the temporary certificate of occupancy, are over-referred by 20%, and target full occupancy within 60 days of TCO, with SHRA paying the subsidy within 30 days of move-in. The 2023 City-County Affordable Housing Plan (SHRA, SSF, City, County) tracks a 649-unit PSH pipeline and a proposed joint PSH fund.

program_name: County Fund for Housing (CFH)
administering_agency: Sonoma County Community Development Commission (CDC)
typical_award_size: FY 2026-27 NOFA: $8,000,000 available (up from $1,500,000 in FY 2025-26 and $1.5M in FY 2024-25). FY 2025-26 awards: Freebird Development, Healdsburg, 42 units, $1,340,417; Burbank Housing, Guerneville, 21 units, $159,583. Minimum loan $100,000; maximum limited to one program year's funds unless the Board commits future years. Since 2003 the fund has invested over $24M in more than 550 homes.
per_unit_cap: No fixed cap; CFH-assisted unit count is set using the HOME per-unit subsidy limits (0-bdrm $153,314 to 4-bdrm $303,490 as of Sept 2021).
affordability_requirement: Rental: all assisted units affordable 55 years, initially to very low income (50% AMI), may float up to low income (80% AMI) on turnover. Priorities: most units at lowest incomes, geographic distribution across cities and unincorporated area, Housing Opportunity Sites, integration with health and human services, PSH and special needs. Homeownership: first-time buyers at or below 120% AMI with 20% of units at 80% AMI.
next_deadline: FY 2026-27 NOFA issued Feb 21, 2026, applications due April 3, 2026 (mandatory TA workshop March 4 or 5), CD Committee recommendations May 13, Board adoption July 7, 2026. Next NOFA expected late February 2027 with an early April deadline; projects ready to proceed to construction get preference.
layering_notes: Sonoma's main local gap source, capitalized by County General Fund, Reinvestment and Revitalization Funds (former RDA), developer in-lieu fees from the residential Affordable Housing Program, non-residential Workforce Housing fees, countywide transient occupancy tax, and loan repayments. Residual receipts loans structured to be compatible with LIHTC investor requirements; interest set by the Commission. Awarded in one annual NOFA together with HOME, CDBG, ESG and LMIHAF so applicants file once. Funds may go to projects inside cities only where the city has a RHNA Sharing Agreement with the County (shelters and congregate facilities exempt). Sponsors must comply with the County Living Wage Ordinance; the policy is silent on prevailing wage, so the Labor Code 1720(c)(6)(E) below-market-loan exemption may apply unless HOME or CDBG is also used. The County does not act as a conduit bond issuer; recent Sonoma deals used CMFA (Burbank Housing $8.12M) and CalHFA. CFH awards are typically $1M to $3M and are counted as local leverage for CTCAC tiebreaker and CDLAC readiness.

program_name: HOME Investment Partnerships Program, Sonoma Urban County
administering_agency: Sonoma County Community Development Commission (CDC) for the Urban County
typical_award_size: FY 2026-27 estimate: HOME $743,322 plus CHDO set-aside $99,090 (Consolidated Plan expects about $660,693 per year plus $60,000 program income). FY 2025-26: $495,519 HOME (George's Hideaway, Burbank Housing, $185,519; tenant-based rental assistance $310,000) plus $99,103 CHDO to George's Hideaway.
per_unit_cap: HUD HOME per-unit subsidy limits (24 CFR 92.250).
affordability_requirement: HOME rules: 20% of HOME units at 50% AMI (Low HOME rent), remainder at or below 60% AMI; affordability period 5 to 20 years by subsidy, CDC loan policies extend to 55 years. Ready-to-proceed projects preferred.
next_deadline: FY 2026-27 round closed April 3, 2026. Next NOFA expected late February 2027, applications early April 2027; Board adopts the Action Plan in July. NEPA review and Section 3 and Build America Buy America compliance required before agreement.
layering_notes: Urban County entitlement area = unincorporated county plus Cloverdale, Cotati, Healdsburg, Rohnert Park, Sebastopol, Sonoma and Windsor; Santa Rosa and Petaluma are separate HUD entitlements (Pass 3). Small allocation (well under $1M a year), so HOME is usually a minor layer on one project per year alongside CFH and PLHA. Davis-Bacon applies at 12 or more HOME-assisted units. The County routinely uses HOME for TBRA, leaving even less for development. Programs are awarded in the single CDC NOFA with CFH and CDBG.

program_name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG), Sonoma Urban County
administering_agency: Sonoma County Community Development Commission (CDC) for the Urban County
typical_award_size: FY 2026-27 estimate: $3,145,583 for affordable housing projects, non-housing capital projects and microenterprise assistance, plus $247,872 for fair housing public services (the FY 2026-27 figure includes reprogrammed prior-year funds; the Consolidated Plan expects about $1.66M annual allocation). FY 2025-26: $1.88M total, with $941,605 to the countywide housing rehabilitation program and the rest to infrastructure and child care.
affordability_requirement: Units for households at or below 80% AMI (51% of units in assisted rental projects); affordable housing projects ready to proceed to construction preferred.
next_deadline: FY 2026-27 round closed April 3, 2026; next NOFA expected February 2027 (applications early April 2027).
layering_notes: Urban County entitlement area = unincorporated county plus Cloverdale, Cotati, Healdsburg, Rohnert Park, Sebastopol, Sonoma and Windsor; Santa Rosa and Petaluma are separate HUD entitlements (Pass 3). CDC lists affordable housing projects as a CDBG eligible use, but new construction remains limited by federal rules (CBDO carve-out) and most housing CDBG goes to the CDC's rehabilitation program and off-site infrastructure. Davis-Bacon applies at 8 or more units. Useful for site infrastructure or acquisition-rehab tied to a 4% deal.

program_name: Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA), County of Sonoma
administering_agency: Sonoma County Community Development Commission (CDC) for the County of Sonoma
typical_award_size: FY 2025-26 distribution $979,795 (Burbank Housing Guerneville 21 units $555,795; Habitat for Humanity Sebastopol 4 ownership units $424,000). Separate NOFAs: Sept 10, 2025 for rental or ownership projects (due Oct 30, 2025); Sept 17, 2026 for affordable owner-occupied workforce housing only, $674,360 over the counter. Residual receipts loans.
per_unit_cap: None published; recent rental award about $26,500 per unit.
affordability_requirement: County PLHA Five-Year Plan: 75% to multifamily rental for households at or below 50% AMI, 20% to owner-occupied workforce housing up to 120% AMI, 5% administration. 55-year restrictions.
next_deadline: Rental PLHA next expected in the CDC's fall 2026 or early 2027 NOFA (2025 pattern: September release, Oct 30 deadline); AOWH PLHA open over the counter since Sept 17, 2026 until the $674,360 is exhausted. Geography excludes the City of Santa Rosa and City of Petaluma, which receive their own PLHA.
layering_notes: State formula money with no federal strings; small annual amounts (under $1M) make it a top-up to CFH rather than a primary source. Mandatory technical assistance workshop before applying. Nonprofit and government applicants only. Below-market residual receipts loan, so the Labor Code 1720(c)(6)(E) prevailing wage exemption may apply absent federal funds.

program_name: Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund (LMIHAF), Sonoma County Housing Successor
administering_agency: Sonoma County Community Development Commission as housing successor to the former County redevelopment agency
typical_award_size: Up to $250,000 per year for homeless prevention and rapid rehousing services (FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-27 NOFAs). Fund balance available for all uses $2,509,338 at June 30, 2025; loans receivable $31.2M; FY 2024-25 expenditures $3.84M. Not currently offered for development.
affordability_requirement: Community Redevelopment Law housing provisions (very low and low income); current awards are homeless services, not capital.
next_deadline: Awarded in the CDC annual NOFA (FY 2026-27 closed April 3, 2026; next February 2027). Capital use would require a Commission decision; monitor the housing successor annual report.
layering_notes: Included so the fund is not mistaken for a development source: the County keeps LMIHAF for services and the former RDA Reinvestment and Revitalization money flows into CFH instead. Loan repayments from legacy RDA projects replenish the fund and could be redirected to capital in future years.

program_name: Project-Based Vouchers for Permanent Supportive Housing, Sonoma County Housing Authority
administering_agency: Sonoma County Housing Authority (division of the CDC); jurisdiction is all of Sonoma County except the City of Santa Rosa
typical_award_size: 2025 PSH RFP: up to 100 project-based vouchers for studio, one- and two-bedroom PSH units in new construction or substantial rehab; applications were due June 24, 2025; 20-year HAP contract with automatic 20-year renewal; one-time $500 per voucher administrative fee plus billed-back environmental and legal review. Board of Commissioners committed 150 future PBVs to PSH (Nov 20, 2024) to support Homekey+ applicants. The authority administers about 2,988 vouchers and roughly $45M a year.
per_unit_cap: HUD limits: 20% of voucher funding may be project-based plus 10% more for units serving homeless or other special populations; per-project cap of 25 units or 25% unless units serve elderly, disabled or supportive-services households.
affordability_requirement: PSH for chronically homeless households referred through the Sonoma County Coordinated Entry System under its PSH prioritization policy; HCV income limits.
next_deadline: 2025 RFP closed June 24, 2025. A further RFP for the 150 committed PSH vouchers is to be released 'when funding is available'; no 2026 RFP was posted as of 2026-11-06. Watch the CDC Doing Business page and HUD's 2026 pause on new PBV commitments.
layering_notes: PBV HAP revenue is the operating subsidy that makes Homekey+, MHP supportive units and CFH-funded PSH underwritable in Sonoma; the 150-voucher commitment was adopted specifically to strengthen Homekey+ applications. Santa Rosa projects must use the Santa Rosa Housing Authority (Pass 3). Prior RFPs: 2018 and 2023 general rounds (up to 100 vouchers, $1,000 fee), 2022 existing-housing round (110 vouchers to 8 projects).

program_name: Affordable Housing Program fees (residential in-lieu fee and non-residential Workforce Housing fee)
administering_agency: Permit Sonoma (collection and compliance); fees deposited to the County Fund for Housing administered by the CDC
typical_award_size: Residential: every unit in unincorporated Sonoma County must build affordable units or pay an in-lieu fee graduated by size; 2026 schedule $3,108 for units of 1,000 sq ft or less rising roughly $155 per 10 sq ft (about $19,000 at 2,000 sq ft, about $29,000 at 2,750 sq ft), paid before building permit final.
