administering_agency: City of Corona Housing Services Division
typical_award_size: FY 2026-27 CDBG and HOME investment $1,844,570; about $8.9M expected over the 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan. HOME is mostly programmed to tenant-based rental assistance ($656,979 TBRA, 20 households). HOME-ARP allocation $1,801,873 (as amended July 2025), part committed to 2nd Street ($529,875).
affordability_requirement: Low and moderate income (at or below 80% AMI); HOME rent limits.
next_deadline: Annual Action Plan adopted each spring for a July 1 program year; FY 2027-28 cycle expected to start winter 2026-27. Little HOME is left for development after TBRA; ask Housing Services before counting on it.
layering_notes: Corona is its own entitlement, not part of the County Urban County. CDBG has been used for land acquisition for housing ($600K on 2nd Street). Corona does not qualify for a HOME match reduction. The Action Plan also lists SB 2 PLHA as a resource.

program_name: Corona Affordable Housing Overlay Zone (AHO), Municipal Code Chapter 17.31
administering_agency: City of Corona Planning and Development Department
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. By-right approval for housing projects on AHO-designated parcels that reserve at least 20% of units for lower income households; mixed use allowed if at least 51% of floor area is residential; density per General Plan designation; objective design standards apply.
affordability_requirement: At least 20% of units for lower income households at affordable rent or cost, regulatory agreement for at least 30 years.
next_deadline: Ongoing. Adopted by Ord. 3360 (2023). The Action Plan also proposes a General Plan change to allow 100% residential in Mixed-Use designations with the AHO overlay.
layering_notes: By-right status removes CEQA and discretionary risk, useful for TCAC readiness. Can be combined with Chapter 17.87 density bonus. The 30-year minimum term is shorter than TCAC's 55 years, so the tax credit term governs.

program_name: Corona density bonus housing agreements, Municipal Code Chapter 17.87
administering_agency: City of Corona Planning and Housing Commission and City Council
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Procedures for state density bonus law (Gov. Code 65915-65918) through a density bonus housing agreement that lists incentives, waivers and parking reductions; filing fee set by Council resolution.
affordability_requirement: Gov. Code 65915 thresholds; term of affordability per Section 17.87.060(B).
next_deadline: Agreements are reviewed by the Planning and Housing Commission and approved by Council (e.g., AHDB2023-0002 for 115 units and AHDB2023-0003 for 25 PSH units, July 2024).
layering_notes: No local bonus beyond state law found. Corona has no inclusionary ordinance or in-lieu fee fund, and no local housing trust fund was found. Amended by Ord. 3391 (2024).

program_name: Temecula housing successor assets and remaining former RDA Tax Allocation Bond proceeds for affordable housing
administering_agency: City of Temecula Community Development Department (Housing Successor to the Temecula Redevelopment Agency)
typical_award_size: Remaining Tax Allocation Bond proceeds are available for affordable housing (balance not published in the documents read). Recent local deals: Las Haciendas (132 units, certificates of occupancy 2024) and Rancho Las Bolsas (26 NPLH units).
affordability_requirement: Lower income; bond covenants and LMIHAF rules apply; the City inspects RDA/SARDA-funded projects annually.
next_deadline: No NOFA. The City makes bond proceed information available to developers through the development application process; contact Community Development (Housing and Real Estate Analyst).
layering_notes: Temecula is a CDBG-only entitlement ($606,465 in FY 2026-27, used for public services and capital projects, not new rental construction) and receives no HOME, so these bond proceeds plus City land are its only cash layer. County HOME and PLHA (county records) are the other local options. A housing successor annual report with the bond balance was not found; request it.

program_name: Temecula Uptown city-owned parcel affordable housing RFP (APN 910-262-061, 1.83 acres)
administering_agency: City of Temecula Community Development Department
typical_award_size: City may donate the 1.83-acre parcel in the Uptown Temecula Sports District as its contribution. A June 2025 RFP drew 6 proposals; the City plans to add adjacent City land and reissue in 2026.
affordability_requirement: Intended as 100% affordable (SLA exemption requested), with interest in short to medium term housing for families at risk of homelessness and a mix of unit types and incomes; 55-year covenants expected.
next_deadline: Reissue expected in 2026 per the 2025 Annual Progress Report; not yet seen in Legistar as of 2026-11-08. Watch Council agendas and the City bid portal.
layering_notes: Site sits in the Uptown Temecula Specific Plan (amended July 2026) and can pair with the AHO and density bonus. A land donation counts as a local public contribution in TCAC scoring and tie-breakers.

program_name: Temecula Affordable Housing Overlay Zoning District, Development Code Chapter 17.21
administering_agency: City of Temecula Community Development Department, Planning Division
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. By-right approval on 44 mapped parcels (just over 100 acres, capacity about 2,007 affordable units) at 20 to 30 units per acre for projects reserving at least 20% of units for households at or below 80% AMI; mixed use allowed in Uptown if residential is at least 50%.
affordability_requirement: At least 20% of units at or below 80% AMI, deed-restricted at least 55 years by recorded regulatory agreement.
layering_notes: By-right path reduces entitlement risk. Density bonus is allowed but the AHO caps the base for bonus purposes at 30 units per acre. Regular impact fees (DIF, TUMF, MSHCP) still apply unless deferred under a development agreement (separate record).

program_name: Temecula development fee deferral and reimbursement through development agreements
administering_agency: City of Temecula Community Development Department
typical_award_size: Case by case deferral or reimbursement of City development fees for qualifying senior and affordable projects; Las Haciendas and Rancho Las Bolsas received fee deferrals and new reimbursement agreements were entered in 2025. Amounts not published.
affordability_requirement: Tied to the project's affordability agreement.
next_deadline: Negotiated through a development agreement; contact Community Development early in entitlement.
layering_notes: Housing Element programs commit the City to continue fee deferral and reimbursement and expedited review. Fee reimbursement is a public subsidy for prevailing wage purposes.

program_name: Temecula density bonus, Development Code Section 17.10.020(P)
administering_agency: City of Temecula Community Development Department, Planning Division
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Grants the bonus, incentives, waivers and parking ratios required by Gov. Code 65915, processed concurrently with development plan review.
affordability_requirement: Gov. Code 65915 thresholds.
next_deadline: Applied at entitlement.
layering_notes: No local enhancements beyond state law found. Temecula has no inclusionary ordinance, in-lieu fee fund or local housing trust fund. The Housing Element target is at least two density bonus projects in the cycle.

program_name: Palm Springs city affordable housing gap loans (housing successor LMIHAF and City housing funds)
administering_agency: City of Palm Springs Community and Economic Development, Housing Division (Housing Successor)
typical_award_size: Reported 2026 commitments (from secondary summaries, not opened on the City site): $3,800,000 loan for the 82-unit Redtail project (3% simple interest, 57-year term, residual receipts), a $2,250,000 acquisition loan plus up to $2,500,000 subordinated fee loan for a 110-unit project at McCarthy and San Rafael (January 14, 2026), and a $3,000,000 commitment for a Wakeland senior project (March 2026). Earlier: Monarch Apartments (60 units) received a City loan, fee waivers and a land grant; a prior LMIHAF loan of about $5.97M to WHCHC.
affordability_requirement: Lower income; terms set per project agreement (55-year or longer covenants typical).
next_deadline: No NOFA found; commitments go to Council project by project. Confirm current fund balances in the FY 2024-25 housing successor report.
layering_notes: Palm Springs is a CDBG-only entitlement (FY 2026-27 CDBG about $337,285 for rehab and legal services), so City and successor funds are the local gap layer, stacked with HACR PBVs and the Coachella Valley Housing Catalyst Fund (county records). palmspringsca.gov returns 403 (Akamai) to scripts and WebFetch, and no working Granicus or Legistar host was found; source_url is the 6th cycle Housing Element draft on HCD, which documents the Monarch loan, fee waivers and land grant but not the 2026 loans.

program_name: Palm Springs Affordable and Multi-Family Housing Incentive Program (Resolution No. 24654), impact fee reduction and deferral
administering_agency: City of Palm Springs (Planning and Building)
typical_award_size: Sliding scale reduction of developer fees and development impact fees from 100% to 1% based on the number and share of affordable units; deferral of fee payment to certificate of occupancy; 50% reduction for market-rate apartments; ADU fee reductions.
affordability_requirement: New housing restricted to lower income households for the affordable tier.
next_deadline: Ongoing per the Housing Element; current resolution status and fee schedule not confirmed.
layering_notes: Unusually generous for the Coachella Valley; stack with the City gap loans and the 93.23.17 density bonus. Fee reductions are public funds for prevailing wage. Program described in the 2021 Housing Element draft on the HCD site; the City resolution and current fee schedule could not be opened (palmspringsca.gov 403).

program_name: Palm Springs density bonus, Zoning Code Section 93.23.17
administering_agency: City of Palm Springs Planning Services Department
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Implements Gov. Code 65915-65918 with on-menu and off-menu incentives, parking alterations and waivers; the City Council may approve a density bonus above state limits by resolution with Housing Element findings.
affordability_requirement: Gov. Code 65915 thresholds.
next_deadline: Applied at entitlement.
layering_notes: The Council discretion to exceed state bonus limits is a local enhancement. No inclusionary ordinance or local housing trust fund was confirmed. Code read on the zoneomics mirror.

program_name: Indio density bonus (Zoning Code Section 1.01.05(E) and Municipal Code Chapter 154)
administering_agency: City of Indio Community Development Department
typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Qualifying projects may apply for a density bonus, incentives and concessions consistent with Gov. Code 65915; Chapter 154 adopts state density bonus regulations by reference.
affordability_requirement: Gov. Code 65915 thresholds.
next_deadline: Applied at entitlement.
layering_notes: No local enhancement found beyond state law. No local housing trust fund, inclusionary ordinance or in-lieu fee fund was confirmed for Indio (see the trust fund record). The 2021 Housing Element noted Chapter 154 only references state law and committed to an implementing update (Program 9). Coachella Valley Housing Coalition is the main local nonprofit developer.

program_name: Indio Housing Authority housing successor LMIHAF and City or Housing Authority owned downtown sites
administering_agency: Indio Housing Authority (Housing Successor) and City of Indio Housing and Neighborhood Services Division
typical_award_size: Older SB 341 reports (FY 2019-20 and FY 2020-21, seen only in search snippets) put the housing successor portfolio at about $7.2M, mostly loans such as Horizons at Indio senior housing (about $3.7M) and a SERAF loan from the Successor Agency. The Housing Element sites inventory includes 32 downtown parcels owned by the City or the Housing Authority, available for development agreements, land write-downs and fee deferrals.
affordability_requirement: LMIHAF rules; project-specific covenants.
next_deadline: No NOFA found. Contact Housing and Neighborhood Services about the current LMIHAF balance and downtown parcels.
layering_notes: Recent Indio affordable deals (Arroyo Crossing I, Avenue 44) lean on County PLHA loans ($500K and $2M per County CEQA notices) and the Coachella Valley Housing Catalyst Fund (county records). indio.org returns 403 to scripts and WebFetch, the Legistar site has no data, and no Granicus host was found; source_url is the 6th cycle Housing Element draft on HCD, which describes the land and incentives.

program_name: Indio Local Housing Trust Fund and inclusionary housing ordinance (Housing Element Programs 11 and 21, not established)
administering_agency: City of Indio Community Development Department and Finance
typical_award_size: No funds. The Housing Element committed to explore a Local Housing Trust Fund and dedicated revenue (commercial linkage fee, inclusionary in-lieu fee or a tax) in year 2 and to evaluate an inclusionary ordinance in year 3.
